title: Resource quality and quantity management processes

lessons.title: Workplace tasks for resource management
lessons.html:
What this work experience covers

In this workplace module you carry out resource management on a working aquaculture farm under the guidance of a supervisor or mentor. You must show, over a period of real work, that you can keep water, air, feed, consumables and equipment at the right quantity and quality.

Typical workplace activities

  • Daily inspection of the water supply: source levels, flows to units, pipework and plumbing, inlet and outlet screens.
  • Monitoring aeration and oxygen supply, and testing alarms and standby power.
  • Taking and recording water quality readings and reacting to out-of-range values.
  • Receiving, inspecting, storing and issuing feed; keeping stock cards.
  • Managing consumables such as salt, lime, disinfectants, reagents and fuel.
  • Inspecting, cleaning, repairing and storing nets, baskets, crates, graders and tanks.
  • Reporting faults and arranging repairs.

Planning your workplace learning

  1. Agree with your mentor which units and resources you are responsible for.
  2. Get copies of the farm's procedures, target ranges and record sheets.
  3. Agree a schedule: daily, weekly and monthly tasks.
  4. Agree how and when your mentor will observe and sign off your work.

Working safely

Resource work involves water, electricity, chemicals and lifting. Lock out power before working on pumps or aerators, use earth leakage protection, wear gloves and eye protection with chemicals, lift correctly, and never work alone in deep water. Follow the OHS Act 85 of 1993 requirements as applied in the farm's safety rules.

Dealing with real problems

On a real farm things go wrong: a borehole pump trips, a feed delivery arrives damp, a screen tears during a storm. These events are valuable learning. Handle them by the procedure, record what happened and what you did, and discuss with your mentor what could prevent a repeat.

lessons.title: Building your portfolio of evidence
lessons.html:
Evidence that you are competent

Your assessor needs proof that you consistently manage resources correctly, not just once. Collect evidence throughout the placement.

Evidence types

EvidenceExample
Completed recordsDaily resource sheets, water quality logs, feed stock cards, equipment fault log
Mentor observation reportsSigned checklists of you inspecting screens or receiving feed
CalculationsFlow measurements, reorder points, feed requirements
Incident reportsA pump failure and how you responded
ReflectionsShort notes on what you learned and would do differently

Quality of evidence

  • Authentic: your own work; never copy records or sign for tasks you did not do.
  • Current: from this placement.
  • Sufficient: enough examples over time to show consistency.
  • Relevant: linked to the tasks in this module.

Remove or blank out confidential business figures if the farm asks, but keep the evidence meaningful.

Explaining your decisions

Be ready to explain to the assessor why you acted as you did: why a reorder point was set at a certain level, why you rejected a feed batch, why you increased aeration before a hot night. Understanding the reasons shows you can manage resources when conditions change.

Improving the system

A strong portfolio also shows improvement. If you notice repeated screen blockages, feed spoilage in one corner of the store or regular stock-outs of a reagent, propose a change, trial it with your mentor's approval and record the result.

Key points

  • Agree responsibilities, procedures and sign-off arrangements with your mentor.
  • Carry out daily, weekly and monthly resource checks.
  • Handle real problems by procedure and record them.
  • Collect authentic, current, sufficient and relevant evidence.
  • Be able to explain the reasons for your decisions.
